sections.text: Darkness, stagnation, folly and infatuation are the result of the dominance of Ignorance, O joy of the Kuru-clan!
यदा सत्त्वे प्रवृद्धे तु प्रलयं याति देहभृत्।
When Purity prevails, the soul on quitting the body passes on to the pure regions where live those who know the Highest.
When Passion prevails, the soul is reborn among those who love activity; when Ignorance rules, it enters the wombs of the ignorant.

We had been discussing Gunatraya Vibhaga Yoga, Yoga of the three gunas. We have concluded that these are the qualities of Prakriti. These three gunas make the Prakriti what it is.
These three gunas come from Maya. Ishwara, in control of Maya, creates Prakriti through Maya. That which is not then appears to be there.
This world of plurality appears to be there. In reality, there is only singularity exist. This Maya creates this Prakriti by three gunas, the Sattva, Rajas and Tamas.
So everything in this Prakriti has these three gunas. If you take the basic building block of our universe as the atom, the atom obviously has inertia. It has activity, and it has some awareness.
From my perspective, the atom remains in its space and time because of inertia. If the atom doesnt remain in space and time, theres nothing you can do about it. We also know that even though it looks inactive, it has extreme activity inside -- the electron swirling around the neutron or proton within the nucleus.
So there is Rajas, and there is Tamas, which is inertia. Tamas keeps the atom in its shape and its existence in space and time. The atom also knows what to do when another atom comes in contact with it, which creates this Prakriti. So right from the basic building block to ourselves, these three gunas are existent.
We obviously are not really concerned about the Prakruti as the universe right now. We are concerned about the Gunas which are manifesting in my internal instrument. Because the goal of my spiritual quest, as we all learned over and over and over again, is cleansing my internal instrument, which is the mind and intellect.
This mind and intellect, when in action, will obviously manifest one guna or another as more predominant. My mind and intellect is nothing but the impressions of my experiences and the transactions in this world. This experience, living its impression, will either make my thoughts more Satwik, more Rajasic, or more Tamasic.
Under the sway of these experiences with the world outside, my internal instrument is constantly transforming from one predominance to another. And thats where we have seen why we should be aware of these gunas. Once I understand how my mind comes under the sway of these gunas, I may be able to train my mind in a manner that will be more beneficial in my spiritual evolution -- in my journey from this limited being to the unlimited being.
And therefore we are also concerned that this life is not long enough. Im trying to attain something but my body doesnt give cooperation and it falls apart prematurely when I have not achieved my goal. The verses we have been seeing say this is a continuity.
This life is nothing but one link in a chain -- the continuity of links which is your existence. And as this limited being, my existence is more at the subtle instrument level than at the external instrument level. This external instrument will die and perish when it has run its course.
The internal instrument will continue. It has gathered experience from the past lives, gathering experience in this life and will continue into the next. So the question is, what happens when I leave this body? The last three verses deal with that.
And Hinduism is the only faith that very systematically deals with the afterlife -- whereas most other faiths and most other schools of thought in this world do accept that there is a life after this life. So the verses you have seen address: what happens? What will be my destination when I leave this station of life? The first verse says, what happens if my mind is in a sattvic mood? Yada sattve pravruddhe tu pralayam yati deha bhrit -- uttama vidam lokan amalan pratipadyate. If my mind is in a sattvic mood of predominance at the time of my leaving, I will reach the world of the highest.
I will go to an environment which will aid my journey from this limited being, the Jiva, to the higher being. So what happens at the time of my death? I may be comatose, I may be in pain, so my mind cannot consciously think about anything. But remember what happens when you go to deep sleep.
Last night when you went to sleep -- youre not necessarily in the same mood every night, nor even aware of when you went to sleep. But the next morning when you wake up, youre basically the same person who went to sleep the night before. An architect going to sleep is not going to wake up as a surgeon the next morning just because the night before he was watching ER.
Hes going to wake up as an architect, because all his life he has accumulated the experiences of an architect. His mind has predominantly become an architectural mind. So when I wake up the next morning, no matter what show I saw on TV last night, my mind will start where I left off.
It may be that at the time of death I am not aware. But the subtle tendencies which my mind has gathered will take me to that world. We dont remember experiences -- even something about what I did in my childhood.
I dont remember what happened in my youth -- a few things here and there we remember. But the tendencies we gathered made me who I am today. My across-the-street neighbor used to take me to Gita class.
I really had no interest whatsoever, but because I couldnt say no, I went with her. That Gita class led me to Gita class today. So the tendencies we gather -- we may not remember anything about them, but the experience of gathering those tendencies creates the sattvic mood or rajasic mood or tamasic mode, and we carry on.
So it says one who dies with a sattvic predominance of mind will go to the world of the highest. The Puranas say it is Brahmaloka -- a place of abundant happiness, very little sorrow or no sorrow, and abundance of creativity. The world of creativity.
Somebody who revels in creativity and gets joy out of that creativity. The next verse says Rajasi pralayam gatva Karma sangi su jayate. If all my life experience was rajasic -- in business and whatever else -- obviously when I die, my mind is still in that mode.
Im not carrying any memories of the experiences, but Im carrying the tendency of those experiences with me. Maybe the last 15 days of my life Im completely comatose. But that just the connection with the body is disconnected.
Mind in its own remain in its own health. And when it leaves, it carries those tendencies with it. So what Im going to do is look for an environment where I can exhaust my vasanas -- my tendencies for being active.
So I may be born in a businessmans house. Karma sanghi su Jayate. Such a person gets an environment, a world of action, where he can exhaust his vasanas for actions. The Lord is very compassionate.
The Lord of this universe, my own Lord, is very compassionate -- He only gives me what I want. If I want knowledge and creativity and awareness about myself, He will give me that. If I want actions, He will give me that too -- He will give me an opportunity to exhaust my vasanas.
Tatha pralinas tamasi mudha yonishu jayate. But if for some reason all my experience of life has been Tamas, then Ill go to the mudha yoni. And mudha yoni is one which is not aware of anything -- the animal kingdom and plant kingdom.
Now obviously we are animals as well, but we are somewhat evolved in that we are aware of things. But if I am not really comfortable progressing in this world, sometimes I may be put in a position where I can be more comfortable in a simpler environment. What is the right thing to do then? Change that environment.
Go back to where I feel comfortable, so I can start my progress appropriately from there. I dont know about here, but in India they sometimes will put you back in the fifth grade and say, well, lets put him back in the fourth grade because that will be the most comfortable. See, its not a punishment.
The Lord never punishes you for your own actions. You only punish yourself for your own actions. Once the mudha yoni is what Im most comfortable with, Bhagavan says, go back, start all over again from there and go further.
And the next verse says Karmanaha sukritasya ahuhu satvikam nirmalam phalam. So what am I supposed to do? Am I just simply programmed, and by chance the experiences Im having in this world will make me either Tamasic, Rajasic, or Sattvic? You do have a choice. Very little, but you have a choice.
And the choice is Karmanaha sukritasya ahuhu satvikam nirmalam phalam -- the result of good action is pure and Sattvic. Rajasa tu phalam dukkham -- the result of Rajas is dukkham, sorrow. And Ill tell you, we have difficulty accepting that.
If thats the case, well all stop acting. But remember, we are not in a business class. We are not in any kind of social reform class.
We are in a class to reform our own mind. In your own mind, you can try it yourself -- put in a spreadsheet what you have done and what the final outcome was of that action. In the end, there will be more pain than what you gained out of that action.
Oh boy, that was a project from hell. But we were dying to get that project. Because in the end this interaction with this world create frictions and the frictions create pain.
The result is always more pain and little happiness. And therefore Vedanta also calls this world Dukkhalaya -- the house of pain. Now this is not to discourage people from doing what they are doing.
This is for you to know, for your mind, what is good. For my mind to remain in equanimity -- if I attach myself to this world, there is nothing but pain. If I attach to good actions, selfless actions, Karma Yoga, the results are sattvic and pure.
Tamas Agnanam Tamasah phalam -- very obvious. If I am completely in Tamas, what is the result? So you decide what you should do. The only thing you have in your hand is your own actions.
Nahi kashchit kshanam api jatu tishthati akarma krit -- you cannot stand for any minute without acting. Good actions will lead to a Sattvic environment. So, of course, everyone wants to do that.
Sattvat Sanjayate Jnanam -- so what happens when I do good actions? Well, people praise me and say Rajan is a good person. No, he said, thats not your goal -- thats actually a detriment to you. The more people praise you, the more your ego gets hardened, and the more criticism you attract.
Durijan Niire Rakhi Angan Kuti Chabai Binapani bin Sabana Nirmal kare Sadh. Sattvat Sanjayate Jnanam -- but why? Im doing good actions because I want sattvic thoughts and a sattvic mood. And whats the result of that? Ill have knowledge -- knowledge about my own self, what my goal is, and how to get there.
Sattvat Sanjayate Jnanam Rajaso Lobha Eva Cha -- he said, do you mean to say this man of action that everybody talks about is not good? This dynamic man of action, if hes driven by his own gains, the result will be greed. Lobha -- greed. We had this hedge fund manager Rajaratnam, who was a billionaire.
He must have come with $8 in his pocket from India. He was a multi-billionaire. But where is he today? Why do you need all those billions and then still have to do something which is illegal?

These verses reveal the profound consequences of which guna predominates at the moment of death, and, by extension, throughout life. Verse 13 lists Tamas symptoms: aprakāśa (absence of light), apravritti (inactivity), pramāda (heedlessness), and moha (delusion). But the teaching goes deeper: verses 14-15 explain that one who dies in a sattvic state reaches uttamavidām lokān amalān, the pure worlds of those who know the Highest. One who dies in Rajas is reborn karmasangishu, among those attached to action. One who dies in Tamas enters mūdhayonishu, the wombs of the deluded. This is not punishment but natural consequence, like an architect who, regardless of what TV show he watched last night, wakes up still an architect because that is what his mind has become through accumulated tendencies.
The teaching offers compassionate wisdom here: the Lord gives each soul exactly the environment it needs to exhaust its vasanas (tendencies). If you crave activity, you get an active life. If you crave knowledge, you get opportunities for wisdom. This is Lords compassion, not punishment. Today, ask yourself honestly: What tendencies am I cultivating? If you were to die tonight, what would the predominant texture of your mind be, clarity, restlessness, or dullness? The beautiful news is that you have choice: karmanah sukritasya āhuh sāttvikam nirmalam phalam, the fruit of good action is pure and sattvic. Right now, in this moment, you can choose actions that cultivate Sattva. What one small choice can you make today that moves your baseline toward clarity and knowledge?
